stem: A UAP reports a heart rate of 118/min for a previously stable client after the RN delegated routine vital-sign measurement. What responsibility remains with the RN?

options.A: The UAP assumes responsibility for interpreting the abnormal result and deciding the clinical follow-up.
options.B: The RN must always repeat the heart rate personally before any other assessment or follow-up can occur.
options.C: The UAP should determine whether ECG testing or healthcare-provider notification is needed.
options.D: The RN evaluates the reported change, obtains additional assessment data as clinically indicated, and determines the appropriate follow-up.

rationale: NCSBN/ANA delegation guidance states that the licensed nurse retains responsibility for supervision and evaluation of delegated care. The delegatee is expected to communicate patient status and may not independently make decisions or modifications outside the delegated activity without consulting the licensed nurse. A newly abnormal vital sign therefore requires RN evaluation and clinical judgment; the RN may obtain additional assessment data as indicated, but no universal rule requires personally repeating every delegated measurement before any other action.
educational_objective: After delegated data collection reveals a new abnormal finding, the RN retains responsibility for assessment, clinical judgment, supervision, evaluation, and appropriate follow-up.
source_organization: National Council of State Boards of Nursing (NCSBN) and American Nurses Association (ANA)
source_version_date: Effective 2019-04-29; current NCSBN delegation resource rechecked 2026-08-16
source_locator: Licensed Nurse Responsibilities → communication; Right supervision and evaluation; NCSBN Delegation page → jurisdictional-law caveat.
source_claim_supported: The licensed nurse remains responsible for supervision, follow-up, and evaluation; the delegatee must report patient status and not independently modify the activity or make decisions outside delegated authority. Jurisdictional rules still govern delegation.

source_original.stem: A UAP reports a heart rate of 118/min for a previously stable client after the RN delegated routine vital-sign measurement. What responsibility remains with the RN?

options.A: The UAP assumes responsibility for interpreting the abnormal result and deciding follow-up.
options.B: The RN should repeat the heart rate before taking further action because delegated vital-sign findings require direct RN confirmation before clinical follow-up.
options.C: The UAP should determine whether ECG testing or provider notification is needed.
options.D: The RN must evaluate the reported change, obtain additional assessment data as needed, and determine follow-up.

source_original.rationale: Delegating measurement of routine vital signs does not transfer the RN's responsibility for nursing assessment, clinical judgment, supervision, and follow-up. A newly abnormal result requires the RN to evaluate the change and decide what additional assessment or escalation is needed, within the jurisdiction's delegation rules and facility policy.
source_original.source_detail: NCSBN National Guidelines for Nursing Delegation — responsibilities of delegating nurse/employer/delegatee; licensed nurse retains responsibility for supervision, evaluation and nursing judgment under applicable jurisdictional law. Current NCSBN delegation guidance at exact URL; currentness rechecked 2026-08-15. NCSBN first-check: Client Needs — Safe and Effective Care Environment — Management of Care; Assignment, Delegation and Supervision; prioritization/continuity/client rights as applicable. 2026 NCLEX-RN Test Plan; effective 2026-04-01 through 2029-03-31; currentness rechecked 2026-08-15.

correction_summary: Retained the delegation construct and key. Removed the unsupported universal rule in distractor B that every delegated abnormal vital sign must first be personally repeated by the RN; final wording preserves RN assessment/judgment responsibility while allowing clinically indicated data collection.

audit_findings.clinical_category: RN delegation — supervision/evaluation after abnormal delegated data
audit_findings.source_authority: Current NCSBN delegation resource and NCSBN/ANA national guideline.
audit_findings.currentness: 2019 joint guideline remains the current NCSBN-linked national delegation guidance; page rechecked 2026-08-16.
audit_findings.exact_locator: Licensed Nurse Responsibilities and Right supervision/evaluation directly support D.
audit_findings.claim_audit: No state-specific UAP task permission is universalized; the stem assumes routine vital signs were validly delegated and tests what remains with the RN.

distractor_audit.A: Improperly transfers nursing judgment to UAP.
distractor_audit.C: Improperly transfers clinical escalation decisions to UAP.

audit_findings.ambiguity_second_answer: Only D preserves RN evaluation/judgment without inventing a mandatory repeat step.
audit_findings.blueprint: Direct NCSBN Assignment, Delegation and Supervision mapping.
audit_findings.independent_second_pass: Confirmed jurisdictional variability is respected and the item does not claim all UAPs universally may take vital signs.
